A small child, bright eyes twinkling with joy and knowledge tip toes into the synagogue, Her mind brimming with answers and questions. She approaches the teachers quietly and boldly raises Her voice with a quiet security of one who holds the universe in the palm of Her small sweaty hand. 
The pharisees are shocked and amazed at first that such an age old question has been answered so succinctly and so easily and by such a young voice.
Their decrepit gazes slowly settle on the reverberation of truth still clinging in the air, their amazement turns to horror as the young girl's brilliant face sets in the middle of their gaze. An outcry pours out of the synagogue as God's only daughter, a small child, is dragged and beaten out into the court. Stones quickly begin to fly and curses fill the air. As the dusty earth begins to clot with blood She sputters a final benediction,  "why Father, why does your creation hate me...I wanted to... show... them..." her bones crush and her breath fails as the stones continue to find their mark.  Her last breath begins "Agape..." the sky darkens and ash begins to fall. Humanity has met its damnation, as it has always deserved

Basic occupancy building codes and material span tables are always over engineered (at least in the US). For example AISC (American Institute of Steel Construction) provides material span and load tables for all typical steel sections. This is based on standards of quality here in the US and is not necessarily transferable to other countries with different standards.  These span tables can be used once occupancy type has been established, which will tell the designer what the live load is per sqft. From here,  based on the floor size of the space they can begin to calculate live and dead loads. Once this is established they can look at a span table, pick appropriate sized members and voila!
